To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

instillation of a particle containing iron into the lung of a human subject results in an increase in the concentrations of ferritin and lactoferin in the lung lavage fluid and that this increase in these two proteins is accompanied by a decrease in the concentration of transferrin in the same lavage.

instillation of iron into a human bronchus is associated with an increase in the concentrations of L-fertitin, lactoferrin, and transferrin receptors in the lower respiratory epithelium and a decrease in transferrin concentrations.

the human respiratory tract responds to an iron-containing particles with increased concentrations of ferritin and lactoferin and a decrease in the concentration of transferrin, all of which are consistent with a decrease in the amount of catalytically active iron.

the human respiratory tract responds to an iron-containing metal particle by increasing ferritin concentrations, which is a protective response.
